Definition: of Hebrew origin (compare H2067); Zebedæus, an Israelite:--Zebedee.
BiblicalUsage: Zebedee is the father of James and John, a fisherman of Galilee who was mending his nets when Jesus called his sons. The Gospels show him sitting in the boat while his sons leave everything to follow Jesus, and years later his sons are still named as the sons of Zebedee, even at the lake where the risen Lord appears.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Zebedee matters because he let his sons go when Jesus called, and a father's faith is often shown in what he releases. His sons became pillars of the church, and their father's name is carried with them everywhere they go.
RelatedPeople: Zebedee; James, Son of Zebedee; John the Apostle; Jesus
